title: Unified function-calling safety shim + stream-aware retry strategy across SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: SDK consumers are increasingly using function/tool calling features across Python/TS/Go. Current SDK layers validate schemas inconsistently, have divergent retry behaviors for synchronous vs streaming responses, and provide poor ergonomics for partial/streamed function results. This causes production surprises (schema validation errors surfaced late), inconsistent retry semantics, and fragile user code when streaming resumes or when functions are invoked with side effects.

Goal: Deliver a cross-SDK "invoker shim" pattern and a small, shared design that: 1) centralizes declarative function schema validation (compile-time / runtime friendly), 2) surfaces a consistent invocation primitive that is stream-aware and supports safe retries, idempotency hints, and resumability, and 3) ships examples and lints for Python, TypeScript, and Go that demonstrate best practices.

Proposed solution:
- Schema registry + compact validator: provide a canonical JSON-schema-like shape and lightweight gluing layer in each SDK. Each SDK will include a small validator that is permissive by default but supports a strict mode (reject unknown fields, enforce types) and a coercion mode (string -> number, etc.).
- Invocation shim: expose a single "CallHandle" abstraction that represents a function invocation across sync and streaming flows. CallHandle supports: start(), awaitResult(), streamEvents(), cancel(), and retry(metadata). For streaming responses the shim exposes offsets (byte/token) and event checkpoints to enable safe replay when idempotency is guaranteed.
- Retry coordinator: implement a stream-aware retry strategy that distinguishes three invocation classes: idempotent (safe to retry at any point), checkpointed (can resume from last checkpoint), and side-effectful (no automatic retries; surface explicit user choice). The coordinator will implement backoff, max-retries, and a safety fence that consults the function schema's "side_effect" annotation.
- Cross-SDK ergonomics: Python will provide an async context manager (with CallHandle as async generator for streamed events). TypeScript will return an async iterable + a separate metadata promise for the final call result. Go will expose a blocking CallHandle with a channel for streamed events and a ResumeToken type.
- Examples & lint rules: add examples for an idempotent embedding-like function, a checkpointable multi-step tool (progress updates), and a side-effectful external API mutator. Ship small linters / runtime warnings to flag mismatched validation modes.

Backward compatibility and rollout: defaults will be conservative: off-by-default strict validation, no automatic retries for unknown side-effectful functions. We will provide opt-in SDK flags: "enable_strict_fn_validation" and "enable_stream_retries". Migration guide will include example transforms and a sample app demonstrating resume tokens.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation in Python/TypeScript/Go with feature parity for validator and CallHandle API surface.
- Integration test harness that runs: correct validation behavior, retry behaviors across simulated network interruptions, and streaming resume tests with synthetic checkpoints.
- Documentation: PRD design doc, SDK README examples, and a migration guide.
- Metrics: add telemetry counters for validation_mode, retry_attempts, resume_success_rate.

Security & privacy notes: function schemas may encode sensitive hints (eg. side_effect:true) but no secret material. Ensure validators are safe from DoS via schema complexity limits.

Open questions: 1) canonical schema dialect to standardize on (JSON Schema v7 subset vs compact custom). 2) how to represent partial streamed results deterministically across model/transport changes. 3) whether resume tokens should be user-visible strings or opaque binary blobs.

Links: design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Unified+Fn+Invoker+Design, sample app repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-fn-invoker-examples
